plan.lspNative.title: Native LSP and completion workflow
plan.lspNative.description: Checks real NVDA output, held Braille information, and perceptible menu interaction; LSP content and event sequences already have automated coverage.
plan.lspNative.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. The Python file lsp_features.py is open. Press Escape once; you are then in Normal mode and cannot insert stray characters.
plan.lspNative.status.title: Report the active LSP clearly
plan.lspNative.status.action: After claiming with F12, press F1, wait for all NVDA speech, then press Escape and F10.
plan.lspNative.status.expected: NVDA clearly reports that Pyright is active for the Python buffer. It does not expose a raw Lua or protocol representation.
plan.lspNative.parameters.title: Hold function parameters on Braille
plan.lspNative.parameters.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. The cursor is already on the function name calculate_total. Press Escape once and do not move the cursor.
plan.lspNative.parameters.action: After claiming with F12, hold NVDA, briefly press Shift+P, and release only Shift+P. Keep NVDA held, slowly press l once and then h once; the two parameters must change. Release NVDA and repeat the same held query once without moving the cursor. Then release NVDA and press Escape and F10.
plan.lspNative.parameters.expected: The signature and parameters 1 and 2 are readable on the Braille display and change with l/h while NVDA remains held throughout. Releasing NVDA restores the previous Braille output; the immediate repeated query shows the same parameters again. The fixture has only one signature, so no visible j/k signature change is expected here.
plan.lspNative.completion.title: Operate native completion
plan.lspNative.completion.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. Press Escape once. F3 moves to a prepared completion location and enters Insert mode automatically.
plan.lspNative.completion.action: After claiming with F12, press F3 and then F5. Select several suggestions with Ctrl+N and Ctrl+P, accept one with Ctrl+Y, then press Escape and F10.
plan.lspNative.completion.expected: NVDA reports selected suggestions clearly and without disruptive repetition. Navigation and acceptance respond smoothly.
plan.lspNative.earcons.title: Native completion menu sounds
plan.lspNative.earcons.action: After claiming with F12, press F3 and F5, navigate briefly with Ctrl+N, and close the menu with Ctrl+E. Then press Escape and F10.
plan.lspNative.earcons.expected: Opening and closing each produce their distinct intended menu sound exactly once.
plan.diagnostics.title: Diagnostic output and earcons
plan.diagnostics.description: Checks perceptible Ruff diagnostics, navigation, sounds, and physical Braille persistence. Ranges, sources, and jump targets also have automated coverage.
plan.diagnostics.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. diagnostics.py is open and the cursor is already on the unused import os on line one. Press Escape once and do not move the cursor yet.
plan.diagnostics.navigation.title: Speak and navigate diagnostics
plan.diagnostics.navigation.action: After claiming with F12, press F6 and wait until “Diagnostics ready” is announced. Only then press F7; it reports the diagnostic at the cursor. Slowly press F9 repeatedly and follow “number of total” until the first diagnostic follows the last one. Press F8 once to move backwards to the last diagnostic. Finally press Escape and F10.
plan.diagnostics.navigation.expected: F7 clearly reports a diagnostic for the unused import. F9 reaches every announced number, including multiple diagnostics at the same position, and then wraps to the first; F8 moves backwards to the last. Every key press produces exactly one complete announcement without disruptive delay.
plan.diagnostics.earcons.title: Diagnostic navigation sounds
plan.diagnostics.earcons.action: After claiming with F12, press F6 and wait until “Diagnostics ready” is announced. Only then press F7; it reports the Ruff F401 warning at the unused import. Then repeat F9 with a short pause between presses until the Ruff F821 error for missing_name is announced. Compare the two sounds, then press Escape and F10.
plan.diagnostics.earcons.expected: F401 uses the warning sound and F821 the clearly different error sound. Every key press produces exactly one diagnostic sound without an additional line-crossing sound or disruptive overlap; further diagnostics of the same severity may intentionally sound alike.
plan.diagnostics.held.title: Hold a diagnostic on Braille
plan.diagnostics.held.action: After claiming with F12, press F6, wait for “Diagnostics ready”, and only then press F7. Next hold NVDA, briefly press Shift+E, and release only Shift+E. Keep NVDA held while exploring with NVDA+k/j. Finally release NVDA, then press Escape and F10.
plan.diagnostics.held.expected: The current diagnostic can be explored on Braille while the gesture is held. Releasing it restores the previous Braille output.
plan.focus.title: Focus isolation and fail-open behavior
plan.focus.description: Checks actual Windows Terminal ownership and return to normal terminal behavior, which test doubles cannot reproduce completely.
plan.focus.workflow.title: Distinguish claimed and unclaimed terminal tabs
plan.focus.context: You initially are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. Press Escape, claim exactly this tab with F12, and leave Neovim open. The middle part needs a second Windows Terminal tab showing an ordinary PowerShell prompt.
plan.focus.workflow.action: Use the plus button or profile menu to open a second Windows Terminal tab with PowerShell. Do not start Neovim or press F12 there. Check ordinary input and navigation without submitting a command. Return to the original tab, press Escape and F10 in Neovim, then check ordinary input and navigation again in the PowerShell view that reappears there.
plan.focus.workflow.expected: The second unclaimed tab keeps NVDA's normal terminal behavior and receives no Neovim output from the first tab. After F10, PowerShell in the original tab is immediately usable normally as well; no Braille output is stuck and input is not blocked.
plan.completionPlugin.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. The Python file is open. Press Escape once. F3 moves to a prepared completion location and enters Insert mode automatically.
